items.title: Deep learning
items.abstract: Deep learning is one of the most significant methods in modern artificial intelligence. Its power is that it is capable of automatically finding features and appreciating intricate patterns previously very hard to reproduce. The development of the field proceeded in stages: beginning with perceptron models of the mid-twentieth century, passing through moments of abandonment and resurgence, and more recently reaching some sorts of transformer architectures. On the way, it was necessary for the researchers to overcome challenges such as vanishing gradients and the enormous computational expediency of training big models. A breakthrough arrived in the 2010. Improved hardware, new training methods, and the availability of huge datasets enabled deep learning to take off in practical applications. Convolutional neural network reimagined computer vision and recurrent neural network along with long short-term memory networks enabled sequence modelling as in language and speech. Transformer models incorporating attention mechanisms reign in natural language processing as we speak constantly zeroing in on new records in performance. It is not only scalable but also malleable that makes deep learning unique. From finance and healthcare to autonomous systems, the impact is obvious. As the area continues to grow, it is bound to continue as a key player in the course of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: As deep learning continues to develop at a fast pace, the field of medical imaging has also seen significant changes due to new technologies making it possible to automatically analyse large amounts of complex image data with much greater accuracy and efficiency than ever before. In this chapter, we will describe and examine many different deep-teaching techniques used in various imaging modalities such as MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), CT (Computed Tomography), X-ray, Ultrasound, Mammograms, and Dermatoscopic as well as Digital Pathology images. We will also discuss several key deep-teaching architectures including CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks), ViT (Vision Transformer), and GAN (Generative Adversarial Networks), and how these architectures can be used in the performance of standard imaging tasks including Image Classification, Object Detection, Image Segmentation, and Image Registration. Moving forward, from the years 2023 through 2025 there will be greater use of Foundation Models, Multimodal Large Language Models, Diffusion-based Data Generation, Real-time Surgical AI, Explainable Transformers, and Federated Learning for training with Privacy Assurance. Finally, we will provide insight into potential future areas for research including Developing Universal Vision-Language Models, AI-driven Precision Medicine, Developing Generalizable Algorithms, Integration into Clinical Settings, and the Importance of Human-AI Collaboration.

items.title: Deep Learning for Personalized Medicine and Precision Healthcare
items.abstract: The combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and precision medicine could potentially change the way medicine is practiced. In this scenario, advances in precision medicine technology will enable healthcare providers to identify the phenotype of each patient who has a unique β-cell response to treatment, as well as other clinical requirements related to their disease. Using AI, sophisticated computers and techniques can help generate insights and create intelligent systems, thereby giving increased decision-making abilities to healthcare professionals. The latest scientific literature shows that as translational research into this combination of precision medicine and AI becomes more widespread, many of the challenges of implementing precision medicine might be addressed. Specifically, this means considering nongenomic, as well as genomic, factors; patient symptoms; clinical history; and lifestyle data in the complete evaluation and management of each patient, which will provide greater diagnostic accuracy and prognostic ability. One of the important causes of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a common complication of diabetes and has affected many millions of people with diabetes throughout the world. DR, like many complications of diabetes is progressive and typically goes undetected until it reaches a stage of nonpreventable blindness. This chapter describes an investigation of the implementation of state-of-the-art deep learning methods in the detection and classification of diabetic retinopathy (DR). This chapter ends with some promising further research topics, including explainable artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen trust as a mechanism, federated learning as a mechanism to facilitate data privacy, and edge AI as a mechanism to implement rapid on-site screening in underserved healthcare domains.

items.title: Deep Learning Methods for Cardiovascular Disease Detection in CT and MRI Scans
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading health concern worldwide and increase the demand for rapid and accurate diagnostic techniques. Although CT and MRI imaging provide excellent cardiac studies, most analysis is slow and inconsistent when performed manually. Deep learning techniques showed strong potential in providing automated interpretation of images, improving accuracy in segmentation, and enabling the classification of diseases reliably. This review recapitulates recent deep learning approaches using CT and MRI for the detection of CVD: CNN-based, hybrid, and transformer-driven models. It examines the primary barriers to using deep learning methods in cardiovascular medical imaging, including limited access to annotated datasets, transparency of models, and the ability to apply findings from one center to another. The Similarly, the paper proposes several novel approaches for addressing these barriers including federated learning, multi-modal fusion in DL models as well as explainable artificial intelligence. These approaches may greatly facilitate the transition of DL technologies into clinics.

items.title: Defending against deepfake speech attacks via feature dropout and dropin regularization in large audio language models
items.abstract: Deepfakes have raised widespread concern owing to their threats to privacy, security, and societal trust, driving growing research interest in effective detection methods. Audio deepfake detection has moved from handcrafted-feature classifiers to end-to-end deep learning architectures and, more recently, to self-supervised speech foundation models and general-purpose speech recognizers such as Whisper. The use of instruction-following speech large language models (LLMs), of which Speech Audio Language Music Open Neural Network (SALMONN) is a representative example, remains comparatively less explored, and forms the setting of this study. We argue that large language models (LLMs), with their powerful representational and information retrieval capabilities, hold significant potential for this task—provided that relevant audio features are carefully selected and prioritized. To this end, we employ a speech LLM, specifically SALMONN, for deepfake audio detection, incorporating a two-stage training strategy in which Stage 1 injects acoustic-feature awareness into the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters via an auxiliary feature-prediction pretext task (referred to as feature dropin), and Stage 2 performs windowed random retention on the encoder token sequence (referred to as feature dropout) before the final real/fake decision. Our approach achieves an absolute accuracy improvement of 0.188 on the FakeOrReal benchmark and attains state-of-the-art performance on the Automatic Speaker Verification Spoofing and Countermeasures (ASVspoof) 2019 LA subset with an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 0.00496, representing a 33.0% relative improvement over prior methods. Furthermore, the model transfers non-trivially to an out-of-domain artificial intelligence (AI)-generated music dataset (M6), reaching accuracy comparable to a ResNet18 baseline reported in prior study, which we interpret as evidence of transferable audio representations rather than broad cross-domain robustness.

items.title: Deliverable No D3.5 Production Planning & Reconfiguration v1
items.abstract: Deliverable D3.5 Production Planning & Reconfiguration v1 provides an overall status update of two core components developed within the CIRCMAN5.0 project’s Work Package 3 (WP3). They are aligned with WP3’s purpose that is to deliver novel simulation and modelling software to improve process and product manufacturing. The first component corresponds to task T3.4 titled “ML-Assisted Production Planning”, is led by ICCS and is dedicated to the development of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms that support the production planning and resource allocation. The second component corresponds to subtask T3.4.1 titled “Embedded edge computing system for the automatic detection of multi-type defects”, is led by CERTH and is dedicated to the automatic detection of multi-type defects in silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules through the design and development of an on-line embedded Internet of Things (IoT) edge computing system. In this first version of D3.5, the challenges and opportunities associated with the transition towards Industry 5.0 (I5.0) are analysed. Based on the analysis, the adoption of I5.0 principles within Production Planning and Control (PPC) systems is investigated, with particular emphasis given on the incorporation of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques into the sub-processes constituting the PPC systems. Furthermore, D3.5, establishes the conceptual link between the two components to be developed under tasks T3.4 and T3.4.1 and the PPC sub-processes, as well as provides a detailed methodology for their development, evaluation, and validation. Lastly, D3.5 outlines planned future activities including the finalization of the ML automation scenarios followed by the development of the algorithms based on data from CIRCMAN5.0 pilot environments and presentation of the results.

items.title: Design and preliminary psychometric validation of an ergonomics-oriented questionnaire applied to mexican teleworkers in working from home conditions using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses
items.abstract: This paper develops and psychometrically validates a four-factor WFH ergonomics questionnaire and examines its factorial validity and reliability in Mexican teleworkers. WFH studies have gained global attention, yet research linking WFH environments to musculoskeletal discomfort remains limited in Mexico. To address this gap, the questionnaire was developed through comprehensive literature review and digitally distributed to N=202 Mexican teleworkers in the manufacturing sector. The questionnaire was preliminary validated through EFA & CFA analyses using factor loadings for item selection and Scree plot, Eigenvalue and Parallel analysis for factor selection to obtain a refined 12-variable and 4-factor model. Statistical validation involved goodness of fit indices, internal consistency and reliability, and convergent and discriminant validity. Because the CFA was conducted on a non-independent sample, the model fit results may therefore be optimistic. The questionnaire provides a standardized basis for ergonomic risk surveillance among teleworkers, supporting preventive interventions at organizational and national levels.

items.title: Designing an AI-Responsive Early Childhood Curriculum: A Conceptual Framework for Supporting Developmental Learning Trajectories in Preschool Education
items.abstract: Background The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning technologies into education creates new opportunities for personalized learning in early childhood education (ECE). Yet limited research has examined how educators interpret and enact AI-responsive curriculum decisions in preschool settings, particularly in culturally diverse contexts. Purpose This study explores educators’ experiences in designing and implementing AI-responsive curricula and develops a conceptual framework explaining how AI can inform curriculum decision-making for young children without displacing teacher judgment. Method An interpretive phenomenological study was conducted at TK Harapan Bangsa, Makassar, Indonesia, with nine adult participants: six preschool teachers, two curriculum specialists, and one AI tool developer-collaborator whose expert interview supplied technical context. Data comprised two in-depth interviews with each teacher, interviews with curriculum specialists and the developer-collaborator, 18 non-participant observations, and analysis of AI-supported planning documents. MAXQDA 2024 supported data management. Giorgi’s phenomenological method was operationalized through first-order meaning units, second-order interpretive themes, and third-order composite constructs. Triangulation, reflexive memoing, an audit trail, member checking, and peer debriefing supported trustworthiness. Findings Three interconnected constructs emerged. Predictive Developmental Tracking describes AI-supported identification of developmental readiness and possible concerns. AI-Responsive Curriculum Adaptation captures teachers’ active interrogation and contextual modification of algorithmic recommendations. Deep Learning as Pedagogical Scaffold positions AI as a support that amplifies, rather than replaces, professional expertise. Together, the constructs informed the AI-Responsive Curriculum Design (ARCD) Framework. Conclusion The ARCD Framework explains AI-responsive curriculum implementation as a relational process combining predictive insight, ecological sensitivity, and educator agency. It offers implications for curriculum policy, teacher professional development, and ethical AI integration in ECE.

items.title: Detecting LLM-Assisted Vietnamese Writing via Keystrokes under Behavioral Manipulation
items.abstract: We study the robustness of keystroke dynamics for detecting large language model (LLM)-assisted writing. We introduce a Vietnamese keystroke dataset capturing realistic writing modes, including bona fide composition, transcription, and paraphrasing. We also define a behaviorally grounded threat model in which users deliberately alter typing patterns. To implement the threat model, we create behaviorally manipulated variants of the data designed to evade keystroke-based detection. We evaluate four keystroke modeling approaches: temporal and rhythmic representations, and sequential representations modeled with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and TypeNet, under user-independent and context-independent settings. The results show that sequential models outperform feature-based approaches in most cases and that keystroke signals encode discriminative information about the writing process. However, detection is not uniformly robust: transcription is reliably identified, while paraphrasing and adversarially manipulated samples are frequently misclassified as bona fide when not explicitly modeled. To address this, we incorporate adversarial training using behaviorally manipulated data, which substantially improves separability and robustness. These results suggest that keystroke-based detection depends critically on exposure to diverse writing behaviors, and that strong performance under limited conditions does not generalize to realistic or adversarial settings without targeted modeling.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Effectiveness of a Global Occupational Health and Safety Management System Model for Japanese Companies
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To extend a Global Occupational Health and Safety Management System Model for Japanese companies-a hybrid model integrating the ISO 45001 standard with company-wide minimum standards set by headquarters and good practices adapted to local conditions-beyond Southeast Asia, the region covered in the original pilot study, and to verify its long-term effectiveness. METHODS: At a large Japanese manufacturer of construction and mining machinery, we examined, over 2013-2026 (a net 12 years, excluding a 2-year suspension during the COVID-19 pandemic): the development of headquarters functions, and changes in 13 performance-audit item scores at 8 production sites in North America, Europe, and Asia. RESULTS: All 9 headquarters functions were established over approximately 12 years. Total audit scores increased at 6 of the 8 production sites; 2 sites showed no improvement. The largest numbers of sites remained below the target level for risk-reduction measures and risk assessment; together with officer competency, the only item showing no change in mean score, these findings revealed a structural lag in occupational hygiene relative to safety. CONCLUSIONS: The model promoted both headquarters maturation and site-level improvement outside Southeast Asia. Strengthening occupational hygiene will require more direct headquarters interventions, such as expert dispatch and technical support, in addition to standard-setting and auditing.

items.title: Development of natural gas quality tracking technology: From steady-state simulation to intelligent hybrid modeling
items.abstract: With the creation of China’s National Integrated Pipeline Network and the transition to natural gas energy measurement, quality fluctuations caused by multisource gas mixing pose severe challenges to trade fairness and pipeline network safety. As a key technology for achieving accurate energy measurement, natural gas quality tracking has undergone a paradigm shift: from steady-state hydraulic calculations to transient composition tracking, and then to intelligent modeling paradigms that feature mechanism-data-driven collaboration. Through a systematic review of technological developments and an analysis of core algorithms, this paper highlights the core value of this technology, namely, its ability to significantly reduce reliance on online gas chromatographs, thereby providing a technical solution to promote energy measurement at Class B and C station yards. It further explores the new challenges presented by hydrogen-blended natural gas and other novel gas sources, including property calculations, numerical dissipation, and safety assessments. Ultimately, future research on this technology should focus on the deep integration of mechanistic models and artificial intelligence, propelling quality-tracking technology toward high precision, strong real-time capabilities, and wide adaptability. This review aims to provide a theoretical reference and technical support for the development of China’s self-sufficient, controllable natural gas energy measurement system.

items.title: Development of Oral English Production Through Artificial Intelligence Tools in Eight Grade Students at Unidad Educativa Fiscal Bicentenario D7
items.abstract: Modern society is undergoing rapid educational changes driven by technological evolution and rising academic demands, establishing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) as key tools for teaching English as a Foreign Language (EFL). This study evaluates the use of AI tools to enhance oral production (speaking skills) among 107 eighth-grade students (sections A, B, and C) at the *Unidad Educativa Fiscal Bicentenario D7 Vespertino* in Quito, Ecuador. The methodology employed a quantitative, descriptive field study design. Key diagnostic findings reveal that 73% of students struggle with initial oral fluency, and 75% report frequent pronunciation errors. However, 68% state that practicing with AI tools boosts their confidence and significantly reduces communication anxiety when speaking in public. Furthermore, 70% demonstrate high motivation for learning through technological resources. Critical limitations identified include limited instructional time (three hours per week), a lack of independent practice outside the classroom (75%), and recurring connectivity and infrastructure issues (56%). The study concludes that overcoming these barriers and the digital divide requires the design and implementation of low-data adaptive micro-learning modules, independent practice guides, and continuous teacher training workshops.

items.title: Development of RAG-Based Generative AI Application: Application of Generative AI in RAG-Based Web Development
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid evolution of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed the landscape of intelligent web application development. Despite their remarkable fluency, standalone LLMs frequently suffer from hallucination, outdated knowledge, and an inability to reference verifiable, domain-specific information, which limits their reliability in enterprise contexts. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses these limitations by coupling a parametric language model with a non-parametric retrieval mechanism that fetches relevant information from an external knowledge base at inference time. This paper presents the design, methodology, and prototype architecture of a RAG-based generative AI web application intended to demonstrate how retrieval, semantic search, and prompt engineering can be combined with modern web development practices to build context-aware, factually grounded AI systems. The proposed system integrates a document ingestion and chunking pipeline, sentence-level embedding generation, a vector database for high-dimensional semantic search, and a large language model layer responsible for grounded response generation. The web application is designed using a React.js/Next.js frontend, a FastAPI/Node.js backend, JWT-based authentication, and a cloud-native deployment strategy using Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines on platforms such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. The paper reviews recent literature on RAG architectures, compares leading vector databases (Pinecone, FAISS, ChromaDB, Milvus) and embedding models, and surveys contributions from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI, Microsoft Research, Hugging Face, LangChain, and LlamaIndex. Rather than reporting fabricated experimental numbers, this work proposes a rigorous evaluation methodology — covering retrieval accuracy, groundedness, latency, and user satisfaction — that can be applied once the prototype is fully deployed. The study concludes that RAG-based architectures offer a practical, scalable, and enterprise-ready pathway toward building trustworthy generative AI web applications, while identifying open challenges such as embedding quality, context-window constraints, and operational cost that motivate future work in agentic and multimodal RAG systems. Keywords: Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Engineering, Vector Database, Semantic Search, AI Chatbot, Web Development, Cloud Deployment, Enterprise Applications.

items.title: DHCG: Dynamic Construction of Hierarchical Collaboration Graphs for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have demonstrated strong capabilities in solving complex problems across diverse domains. Recently, the dynamic orchestration of agent systems has become an important research direction. However, existing methods suffer from limited composition, misaligned dependencies, and inflexible scale, restricting their ability to adapt to reasoning requirements during execution. To address these limitations, we reframe MAS design as a partially observable Markov decision process, in which both the composition and scale of the MAS are dynamically determined. We propose DHCG, a novel framework that coordinates three modules (Planner, Worker, and Generator) to progressively construct a dynamic hierarchical collaboration graph from scratch based on the query and evolving execution feedback. At each step, guided by feedback, the Planner generates a set of distinct and complementary roles tailored to the current reasoning needs and selectively routes relevant information to each role. It can also finalize the hierarchical collaboration graph early or progressively expand it when additional reasoning is required. We further introduce action-aware preference optimization to train the Planner to make more effective decisions when constructing hierarchical collaboration graphs. We systematically evaluate DHCG across code generation, mathematical reasoning, and domain-specific reasoning benchmarks. DHCG achieves state-of-the-art average performance among the compared methods, improving over the single-agent baseline by 13.06 points and outperforming both static and dynamic MAS baselines by 2.77-8.02 points. Additional experiments further demonstrate its generalization across different Planner backbones and unseen Worker models.

items.title: Differentiating linked cognitive states under task demand and sleep restriction: toward an experimental framework for operational monitoring
items.abstract: Real-world settings involve multiple interacting cognitive states such as mental workload, drowsiness, fatigue, and mind wandering, yet these are typically studied in isolation. A critical question is whether these states can be empirically differentiated given that they share overlapping behavioral and physiological signatures. We investigated whether task difficulty and sleep restriction produce dissociable effects across these states, and whether their response patterns reflect distinct underlying mechanisms or a common cognitive resource using a unified framework. Participants from operational populations (Study 1: n = 40; Study 2: n = 27) performed three complementary tasks (MATB-II, N-Back, and SART) under two manipulations: task difficulty and partial sleep restriction, targeting cognitive load and alertness. Increasing task difficulty degraded performance and increased perceived workload and fatigue across tasks. In contrast, sleep restriction primarily elevated subjective drowsiness and mind wandering, with smaller, task-dependent effects on performance. These findings provide evidence that cognitive and physiological states influencing situational awareness can be differentiated using complementary manipulations and characterized through distinct behavioral and subjective measures. This distinction provides a foundation for future predictive and monitoring approaches in applied settings.

items.title: Digital communication and occupational well-being in 25 European countries
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines the association between digital communication at work and employee well-being, moderated by occupational status and the fulfillment of basic psychological needs. Two studies were conducted to investigate these relationships. Study 1 utilized data from the European Social Survey, encompassing 25 countries ( N = 24,331). Study 2 involved a longitudinal survey of Finnish workers ( N = 1817) collected at nine time points over 6-month intervals from 2019 to 2023. Multilevel regression models were employed to analyze the data. Study 1 found that digital communication positively correlates with job satisfaction in Europe, with a stronger effect observed among lower-position workers. Study 2 revealed that the use of digital platforms was associated with higher work engagement and women reported significantly higher work engagement than men. However, for higher-position office workers, particularly those in supervisory roles, increased use of organizational social media platforms and excessive social media use were linked to decreased work engagement. Several interaction effects indicated that the association between digital communication as well as digital tool use and work engagement and job satisfaction is contingent on basic psychological need satisfaction and occupational status. Organizations should tailor their digital communication strategies to account for employees’ occupational status and work autonomy. This paper addresses a gap in cross-national and longitudinal research on the impact of digital communication on workplace well-being. It provides insights into how digital communication tools differentially affect employees based on their occupational status and psychological needs.

items.title: Digital Marketing and Communication Strategies
items.abstract: This chapter examines digital communication, marketing, and institutional identity in higher education as interconnected organisational domains. It treats digitalisation as the foundation of institutional practice and digital communication as a managerial rather than purely promotional function. Institutional communication is analysed as an integrated process encompassing both external stakeholder engagement and internal communication. The chapter reviews the core platforms that underpin institutional communication, including websites, social media, email, and internal collaboration systems. It argues that strategic effectiveness depends less on the number of channels used than on their governance as a coherent, audience-centred portfolio. It also explores the role of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), podcasts, and EdTech tools, which increasingly combine communication, service delivery, and data generation. The chapter further considers how artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education marketing through personalisation, predictive analytics, and customer relationship management (CRM-)based engagement, while highlighting the importance of trust, transparency, and regulatory compliance. Finally, it argues that successful implementation depends on digital leadership, effective governance, capability development, and staff well-being, all of which shape whether digital transformation strengthens or weakens institutional coherence.

items.title: Digital Research Ecosystems
items.abstract: Digital research ecosystems (DREs) constitute the infrastructure core of contemporary academic scholarship, significantly altering how scientific knowledge is generated, organised, validated, and preserved. This comprehensive academic work provides an exhaustive, multi-layered analysis of DREs as integrated sociotechnical systems operating at the intersection of computational advancement and institutional evolution. It examines the historical shift towards data-intensive science, maps the emergence of the fourth paradigm of discovery, and investigates how these ecosystems support the lifecycle of research data through the operationalisation of open science principles. The structural components of DREs are dissected across multiple layers, emphasising the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and automated knowledge systems in semantic discovery and automated curation. Furthermore, the analysis addresses critical systemic challenges, including technological fragmentation, academic capitalism, data silos, geopolitical digital inequalities, and the delicate ethical-legal tensions surrounding data privacy, surveillance, and security. Finally, it outlines emerging revolutionary paradigms such as Decentralised Science (DeSci) and autonomous, closed-loop research infrastructure, providing a robust theoretical framework for understanding the long-term trajectory of global scientific collaboration.

items.title: Digital transformation, technological innovation, and e-sports: ISSF at a new stage of shooting sport development
items.abstract: In the modern era, the survival of traditional sports disciplines is directly linked to their ability to adapt to a dynamic media environment. The International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) has entered a period of fundamental transformation, shifting from a closed technical discipline toward a high-demand global media product. The central challenge lies in changing the "cognitive perception" of shooting – transforming a process that appears static to an outside observer into an emotionally resonant and technologically accessible spectacle. This article analyzes the key directions of this process. First, it examines the diversification of content delivery through the aggressive scaling of digital presence and the exploration of new platforms. A vital aspect is the technological verification and increased transparency of officiating, achieved through the implementation of VAR objective control systems and "live aiming" shot visualization technologies. The study also investigates the integration of virtual reality and esports as a means of creating alternative "entry points" into the sport via digital simulators. Alongside these developments, the work analyses the associated risks and institutional consequences of this transformation. The implementation of innovations such as AI-driven hit analysis and VR tools fosters the necessary "immersive connection" between the athlete and the fan. This is critical for attracting sponsorship capital, as it allows dry technical data to be converted into engaging content. The findings are based on a comparative analysis of Redtorch reports (SportOnSocial 2025), official ISSF press releases, and current industry publications. items.title: Disciplinary Perspectives on the Relevance of AI Research Assistants for Scholarly Article Discovery
items.abstract: This study explored artificial intelligence (AI) research assistants through the lens of scholars from different disciplines as they interacted with the tools. The goal was to determine whether AI tools provide relevant scholarly literature or prioritize surface-level relevance at the expense of disciplinary depth, and to examine how scholars perceive the usefulness of the tools in teaching and learning. The study used a multiple-phase, qualitative design in which ten scholars from several disciplines completed structured search tasks in each AI research assistant (Consensus, Elicit, SciSpace), followed by semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using qualitative coding techniques, with themes developed through thematic analysis approach. Analysis involved data familiarization, memoing, iterative first and second cycle coding, and the generation and refinement of themes. The findings revealed six themes from the search task diaries and interviews with participants: article coverage varied across disciplines; discipline specific information needs and resource mismatch; a complementary resource for scholarly article discovery; AI summaries technically correct but generic; faculty perceptions on AI tools in student learning; usability and cognitive load considerations. The findings indicate that while most tools surfaced additional research from scholarly journals, they often did not consistently identify seminal literature across the sampled disciplines. AI summaries on the literature were perceived as factually correct but generic. Lastly, participants expressed varied perceptions about the ways in which the tools could be used in teaching and learning contexts.

items.title: Dissecting AI discourse
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the discourse characteristics of AI-generated argumentative essays designed to simulate student writing, comparing them with human-authored texts to explore linguistic variation and its implications for academic discourse. While large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT demonstrate impressive fluency and coherence, questions remain about their capacity to engage in nuanced argumentation and the critical reasoning expected in academic contexts. Employing Biber’s (1988) multidimensional (MD) analysis, this study examines systematic differences between LLM-generated and human-written essays across dimensions of register variation, informational density, syntactic complexity, and persuasion. The results reveal that ChatGPT essays are markedly more informationally dense, context-independent, and abstract, yet exhibit reduced interpersonal engagement and overt persuasion compared with student essays. The paper concludes by reflecting on broader pedagogical and ethical implications for the integration of AI tools into academic writing and corpus-based research.

items.title: Do Chatbots Sound Equally Sure in French and in Arabic? A Pilot Audit of Expressed Certainty in ChatGPT and Gemini
items.abstract: People increasingly ask chatbots about health and public services and pass the answers on to others. Whether they check first may depend on how sure an answer sounds. This pilot audit asks whether the certainty cues that chatbots give change with the language of the question. Ten questions on public health and public services in Morocco were asked once in French and once in Modern Standard Arabic to ChatGPT and Gemini (40 answers). Answers were scored with a bilingual lexicon of hedges and boosters. Both chatbots hedged less in Arabic than in French, and the pattern held under two alternative versions of the lexicon. A model-assisted second coding of 10 answers showed that the lexicon captured boosters well but missed about a third of hedges. With 10 questions and one run each, these results are a first look, not a finding. They motivate a larger audit with repeated runs and human validation.

items.title: Does On-Policy Distillation for Safety Pose Backdoor Risks?
items.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has attracted growing attention as an effective way to transfer capabilities from teacher models to student models. Recent studies further explore OPD as a tool for improving large language model safety with promising results. However, these approaches typically assume that the teacher and training data are trustworthy. In this paper, we uncover an overlooked threat to OPD for safety: a safety-aligned but backdoored teacher can propagate its hidden malicious behavior to an initially clean student. Under our threat model, a poisoning rate as low as 3% results in an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 70% on the distilled student. We further identify two training choices that can amplify this risk. First, increasing the number of training epochs can lead to high ASR even at low poisoning rates. With only 10 poisoned samples, ASR reaches 67% after 16 epochs. Second, the commonly used top-k KL can accelerate backdoor transfer, causing trigger-conditioned harmful behavior to emerge earlier than sampled-token KL in most settings. Alongside these findings, we explore a simple mitigation, Lazy Defense, which clips KL rewards to make student updates less aggressive, limiting aggressive updates and slowing backdoor learning. Experiments show that Lazy Defense delays backdoor transfer in low poisoning rate settings. Together, our findings reveal that OPD can propagate backdoors, highlighting the need to address the safety risks of OPD.

items.title: Does Steering Break Your Model? A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Suite for LLM Steering Methods
items.abstract: Activation steering provides a lightweight and flexible way to control large language model (LLM) behavior. However, effective steering requires more than inducing the intended behavior: it should also limit unintended changes and remain robust across inputs and training data. Existing evaluations cover these dimensions only in fragments. As a result, the trade-offs between efficacy and side effects have not been systematically characterized. We introduce SteerScope, a two-axis, multi-dimensional evaluation suite that jointly characterizes steering outcomes and method properties through 15 metrics. We score target efficacy and side effects on language quality, task capabilities, and safety and reliability, and further assess generalization and data dependence through steering-specific metrics for sample efficiency and sample sensitivity. Rather than comparing methods at a single operating point, we characterize the trade-offs between efficacy and side effects. Under matched models, tasks, and evaluation protocols, we benchmark 23 methods spanning 4 families, including prompting, LoRA, and SFT as baseline methods, and release the suite as an extensible codebase. We find that current activation steering methods do not yet surpass the Prompt Steering baseline in their overall balance between steering efficacy and side effects: across both model scales, no evaluated activation steering method achieves higher efficacy without incurring greater composite side effects. We further uncover a consistent coupling between steering efficacy and side effects. Under OOD prompts, target efficacy is often preserved, whereas side effects tend to become more pronounced, particularly through declines in instruction relevance and fluency. Methods also exhibit sharply different sample-efficiency profiles.

items.title: Drawing the Line: Where AI Guidance and Human Creativity Meet in Emotion-Driven Comic Storyboarding
items.abstract: While generative AI models can produce visually faithful artwork, they often fall short in conveying emotional authenticity--a key driver of human expression. In visual storytelling, particularly comic storyboarding, this gap becomes pronounced: effective storyboards require both technical knowledge (e.g., anatomical accuracy or scenic composition) and emotional insight (from lived experience). We explore how human-AI collaboration can support emotion-driven creativity, where the user's feelings guide generation and emotional resonance is the goal. We present EmoToon, a technology probe that helps non-professional artists generate sketch-like storyboards and iterate on visual ideas. In a controlled study with N=25 participants, we find that AI assistance significantly improves emotional expression, aesthetic quality, and exploration, but reduces users' creative ownership. Our findings offer broader insights for human-AI co-creation in the domain of comic storytelling, emphasizing balance between output quality and user freedom, and raising new challenges for image generation models in this domain.

items.title: Driver Responses to Mismatches Between Expected and Experienced Automated Vehicle Driving Styles
items.abstract: Automated vehicles (AV) can exhibit diverse driving behaviors that deviate from driver expectations. More research is needed to understand drivers’ preferred driving styles when navigating safety-critical situations as well as their responses to unexpected AV driving behaviors. Forty-eight participants experienced simulated automated driving scenarios where an AV navigated a construction zone while exhibiting four different predefined driving styles that varied in terms of cautiousness and efficiency. After each trial, participants provided feedback to adjust the AV’s driving style toward their preferences, which was successfully implemented in 80% cases. Drivers’ trust, workload, voluntary takeover decisions, eye movements, and skin conductance were measured. Overall, participants preferred driving styles balancing cautiousness and efficiency. When AV behavior matched driver preferences, they reported higher trust and more stable visual scanning patterns, while unexpected behaviors were associated with broader ocular scanning. Findings can inform the development of adaptive systems that intelligently modify AV behaviors.

items.title: Early Detection of Brain Stroke using Deep Learning
items.abstract: A stroke results in a serious disability due to sudden disruption in blood flow to the brain, which may cause fatal outcomes and is considered as the topmost cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. The reduction of brain damage along with the recovery of patients has shown potential increase due to accurate and time based diagnosis. The competence of artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning and for stroke detection using data from different sources such as EHRs, EEG, and MRI have been explored in this chapter. Different types of CNN and deep learning models are analyzed to classify various data types along with the identification of stroke signatures. The various advantages which are related with the AI based stroke detection such as timely and faster diagnosis leading to early treatment and higher accuracy which surpasses the traditional methods. Even the chances for remote patient monitoring have been increased due to AI which also has paved the way for incorporating AI in clinical environments without causing any disruption to current healthcare practices. Further, this chapter discusses the potential of using AI in personalized medicine where the risk assessment and treatment plans for the patient can be based on the medical history of the patient. The chapter further discusses about the long term efficacy of using AI models with the ongoing learning by making use of advances in medical knowledge and access to the data. This chapter ensures to guide the researchers and medical professionals with the deep understanding of using deep learning and AI for stroke diagnosis by exploring the potential benefits, challenges and future outlook for the methodology for early store detection.

items.title: Editing by prompt. How professional editors use ChatGPT when revising business texts
items.abstract: Writing technologies shape writing processes and practices. This was true of word processing, speech recognition, and writing with internet-based sources, each of which changed how writers produced and revised text. Generative AI may have an even more fundamental impact because it can participate directly in producing, evaluating, and transforming text. In this study, we examine how generative AI affects the revision processes of professional editors. Six professional editors revised four Dutch business letters with ChatGPT available alongside Word. Using Inputlog process data, ChatGPT interactions, interim texts, and interviews, we reconstructed when and how editors used the model, what revision work they assigned to it, and how generated material entered subsequent editing. Editors used ChatGPT mainly to generate candidate repairs, from complete rewrites to local reformulations, and sometimes to help identify problems in the source text. They differed, however, in when they turned to the model and in how much revision they had already done themselves. Most evaluation, adaptation, and integration still took place in Word. ChatGPT replaced particular revision activities rather than the editing task as a whole. Editors still had to define problems and goals, judge the model’s output, and decide what to retain in the final text. We discuss what these changes mean for how professional revision is organized and for the role of editorial expertise in AI-supported editing.

items.title: EDUCATING PHYSICIANS FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: MEDICAL UNIVERSITIES IN UZBEKISTAN AND SAFE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN HEALTHCARE
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming healthcare delivery, clinical decision-making and health system governance. However, the safety and effectiveness of AI implementation depend not only on technological infrastructure but also on workforce preparedness and institutional capacity. This conceptual study explores the role of medical universities in Uzbekistan in developing competencies required for responsible AI adoption in clinical practice, healthcare management and public health. Drawing on international literature, policy frameworks and national academic discourse, the paper proposes a conceptual model explaining how educational interventions influence professional readiness for safe AI integration. The analysis highlights persistentcompetency gaps, the mediating role of universities in shaping professional attitudes and broader system-level implications of AI literacy programmes. The study argues that competency-oriented educational strategies aligned with national digital health reforms may support sustainable innovation while preserving professional accountability and patient safety.

items.title: Educator and AI agent communication in AI-mediated higher education classrooms: a mini review along the complementarity-substitution axis
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education classrooms has reignited the debate over the role of communication between educators and students. This mini-review synthesizes the role of instructional communication constructs (immediacy, rapport, clarity, and credibility) and the relational functions they deliver in AI-mediated classrooms, based on 32 peer-reviewed studies published after 2023, identified through a large-scale literature search (using Scopus and Web of Science-based indexes, OpenAlex, and ERIC). The findings fall into three main categories. First, educator communication behaviors continue to predict student outcomes; a recent meta-analysis reports a moderate-to-large association (r = 0.443), although the evidence base is concentrated in Chinese and EFL samples. Second, students evaluate AI agents using human communication categories, but a systematic gap emerges in the dimension of goodwill, which is partially bridged by cues of immediacy and politeness. Third, when AI replaces human interaction, negative outcomes related to loneliness and a sense of belonging are observed. These three strands are integrated around the complementarity-substitution axis defined at the level of relational functions; tests of measurement invariance, sample diversity, and longitudinal designs are recommended for future research.

items.title: Emerging Trends and Future Directions
items.abstract: This chapter examines the major emerging trends that are shaping the future of nanoparticle science and selection. It explains that the field is moving beyond conventional one-material, one-function approaches towards nanoparticle platforms that are increasingly multifunctional, adaptive, system-aware, and digitally assisted in their design and optimization. The chapter focuses on three major themes. The first is the rise of next-generation nanoparticle systems, including hybrid and heterostructure materials, stimuli-responsive platforms, layered nanomaterials, porous framework-derived systems, bioinspired nanostructures, and safety-aware designs. The second is the growing integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-intensive methods into nanoparticle discovery, synthesis optimization, characterization analysis, and predictive selection. The third concerns the unresolved research needs and technological barriers that continue to limit broader translation, including scale-up, standardization, reproducibility, long-term stability, toxicity assessment, and realistic benchmarking. The chapter therefore positions future nanoparticle selection as an increasingly hybrid process in which mechanistic understanding, experimental evidence, and computational guidance will operate together rather than separately.

items.title: Emotional resonance and cultural reproduction in digital landscapes: Cross-media practice and social implications of CP culture
items.abstract: This article examines CP (Couple Pairing) culture – the fan practice of imagining romantic relationships between fictional characters or celebrities – on Chinese digital platforms, combining media sociology, platform studies, and cultural economy. Rather than treating Chinese CP culture as sui generis, the analysis first situates it within a longer transnational genealogy that includes slash fiction, Japanese yaoi, Western real-person shipping, and queerbaiting, before specifying what is distinctively Chinese about its present sociotechnical organization. Drawing on eighteen months of digital ethnography across four platforms (Weibo, Bilibili, LOFTER, and Douban), interviews with forty-five stakeholders, and comparative analysis of five media properties, the study develops the concept of “emotional capitalism infrastructure”: the algorithmic, interface, and narrative mechanisms through which platforms convert affective fan labor into economic value while still affording participants genuine emotional and social benefits. Findings show that platform affordances shape which emotional practices become visible, shareable, and commercially actionable, and that these practices mutate as they migrate across platforms rather than remaining platform-bound. Gender emerges as constitutive, rather than incidental, to CP culture’s affective logic, and China’s regulatory environment is treated as one variable among several – alongside industry structure and platform design – shaping this transnational cultural form. The article closes with governance implications that weigh consumer protection against the cultural and psychological benefits CP participation provides.

items.title: Empirical Case Studies of Digital-Era Transformation in Higher Education Management
items.abstract: This chapter presents four case studies that illustrate how digital transformation is enacted in different institutional contexts under the new academic wave. The cases are analytical examples of diverse strategic and governance approaches rather than evidence of effectiveness or performance. The analysis draws on institutional documents, interviews, and study visits. The University of Helsinki and the University of Turku represent two complementary Finnish approaches. Helsinki combines a mission-driven digital humanities platform with institution-wide coordination of artificial intelligence (AI). Turku implements a university-wide digitalisation programme that integrates learning, research, partnerships, and staff development. Laurea University of Applied Sciences embeds digital transformation within its Learning by Developing model, where technology supports authentic and workplace-related learning. Mondragon University follows a technopedagogical and cooperative approach. Digital tools are adopted when they support pedagogical goals and are governed through distributed support structures and shared institutional values. Tamkang University links digital transformation to a long-standing culture of futures thinking through an all-cloud smart campus and an institutional generative AI service. The cases show that there is no single model of digital transformation in higher education. Instead, digital-era strategies take different forms, shaped by institutional history, mission, governance arrangements, and educational values.

items.title: Employee Motivation
items.abstract: Employee behavior, performance and organizational success are profoundly influenced by motivation, which is a dynamic and ongoing process within human resources. Unlike many other HR systems that rely on fixed tools or formulas specific to an organization, motivation cannot be confined to a one-size-fits-all approach. This is largely because employees have diverse needs, expectations, values and personal circumstances. Consequently, strategies that effectively motivate employees in one organization or even within a single department may not yield the same results elsewhere. HR managers face the challenge of recognizing these differences and developing a variety of motivational techniques that address the diverse demands of their workforce. Over the years, various content theories of motivation such as Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory and McClelland’s Need Theory have provided valuable insights into the internal factors that drive individuals. These theories emphasize essential needs such as achievement, recognition, responsibility, personal growth and job security as crucial elements of motivation. Conversely, process theories – including Vroom’s Expectancy Theory, Adams’ Equity Theory and Locke’s Goal-Setting Theory – focus on how motivation is activated by highlighting perceptions of fairness, the clarity of goals, expectations of rewards and the individual’s assessment of outcomes. These theoretical perspectives have been significantly supported by empirical research conducted in India and beyond, demonstrating that motivation is influenced by contextual and cultural factors. Businesses that effectively understand and apply these concepts can develop a more motivated workforce. Devoted and effective employees are often the result of proper motivation. Both intrinsic and extrinsic reinforcers can inspire individuals to excel. Intrinsic motivation stems from internal elements such as autonomy, meaningful work, personal fulfillment and opportunities for learning. In contrast, extrinsic motivation is driven by external incentives like compensation, bonuses, promotions and recognition. It is essential to strike a balance between both types for sustained employee engagement. Ultimately, motivated employees tend to be happier, which directly enhances productivity, creativity and overall performance. Understanding the nuances of motivation is not merely a theoretical exercise for Human Resource Management; it serves as a strategic tool that influences long-term effectiveness, organizational culture and employee retention. When employees feel valued, empowered and supported, they are more likely to contribute positively to organizational success.

items.title: Energy Efficiency Improvement Strategies in Modern Electrical Power Systems
items.abstract: Modern electrical power systems waste between 35 and 55% of primary energy input through thermal generation inefficiencies, transmission and distribution losses, reactive power deficits, and suboptimal demand-side management. This global inefficiency leads to unnecessary carbon dioxide emissions, wasted fuel costs, limited system capacity, and delayed socioeconomic development. As the world moves toward more renewable energy, more distributed generation topologies, and more electrification of transport and thermal loads, it has never been more important to make sure that every joule that enters the electrical network is used as efficiently as possible. This paper provides a thorough academic examination of strategies for enhancing energy efficiency that are relevant to all phases of contemporary electrical power systems, encompassing generation, transmission, distribution, and consumption. The theoretical basis for energy efficiency in power systems has been set, including thermodynamic limits, power factor, conductor losses, and reactive power compensation. The strategies that were looked at include: advanced generation technologies (combined heat and power, ultra-supercritical steam cycles, and integrated gasification combined cycle); high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission and flexible alternating current transmission system (FACTS) devices; smart grid architectures with advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) and volt-VAR optimization; energy storage systems for curtailment reduction and loss minimization; demand-side management (DSM) and demand response (DR) programs; and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) applications for real-time system optimization. A techno-economic analysis shows that using these strategies consistently can raise the overall system efficiency from a typical developing-country baseline of 38-45% to 60-68%. This means that 15-26 percentage points of primary energy can be recovered, and levelized energy savings can be achieved that make investment in all technology categories worthwhile. A structured implementation roadmap is provided, ranking strategies by cost-effectiveness, maturity, and deployment timeline. This is a useful guide for power system planners and policymakers in both developed and developing countries.

items.title: Enhancing LLMs with Cognitive-Affective Personality Inference for Simulating Human Social-Psychological Behavior
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate human participants in social and behavioral studies, yet static persona prompting typically maps a participant profile and an experimental scenario directly to a response, entangling stable dispositions with situation-specific interpretations. To address this limitation, we introduce \textbf{SPIN}, a cognitive-affective personality system-inspired inference pipeline for simulating human social-psychological behavior. Specifically, SPIN implements this structured inference process through three zero-shot LLM calls that compile a task-blind participant core, elicit condition-specific cognitive-affective states, and read out decisions from those states, thereby reusing stable personality structure while routing each trial-specific response through an explicit state representation. We evaluate SPIN on two reconstructed social-psychological study families spanning uncertainty reasoning and pluralistic ignorance, across four base LLMs. Compared with blank, demographic, narrative, and chain-of-thought prompt variants, SPIN consistently delivers the strongest overall alignment performance across base LLMs and study families. Ablations and state analyses further show that both personality compilation and structured state elicitation contribute to the gains, and that the elicited states shift interpretably across informational and normative conditions. These results suggest that structured personality-state inference can improve benchmark-level behavioral alignment beyond richer persona descriptions or generic multi-step reasoning.

items.title: Ergonomics and Human-Centered Design Perspective
items.abstract: Global aging and the growing digital divide among older adults require more accessible and inclusive digital technologies. This study, developed as part of the national project “Age-It—Ageing Well in an Ageing Society,” aims to define design guidelines based on the scientific and methodological approaches of Ergonomics for Design and Human-Centered Design, with a view to improving the usability and acceptability of gerontechnology. The methodology adopted combines a systematic review of the scientific literature using the PRISMA framework, a focus group with people over 65, and a workshop with designers to gather empirical data and multidisciplinary design perspectives. Analysis of the results led to the development of a set of guidelines organized into four specific categories: cognitive, sensory, functional, and systemic aspects. These categories reflect the main challenges associated with the interaction between older adults and technology, taking into account factors such as memory, attention, linguistic comprehension, motor skills, sensory perception, and sociocultural barriers. The proposed guidelines aim to support designers, researchers, and companies in developing physical-digital interfaces and devices that are accessible, understandable, and engaging for older users, thereby promoting active and healthy aging. The contribution combines ergonomics and participatory design, bridging the gap between technology and the needs of older people, and lays the foundations for future applications in the field of digital health.

items.title: Estimation of hydrological drought using regional risk ranking and machine learning algorithms
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrological drought forecasting remains challenging due to non-linear propagation processes, temporal subsurface lags, and strong spatial heterogeneity across river basins. Conventional deep learning frameworks routinely train monolithic global networks across entire watersheds, which often induces parameter dilution and obscures localized recovery dynamics. To resolve these challenges, this study develops a novel, two-stage artificial intelligence framework that integrates density-based spatial risk regionalization with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) deep neural networks. Utilizing multi-decadal anomalies of the Standardized Runoff Index (SRI) and Drought Deficit Volume (DDV), sub-basins in the Zengwen River Basin are first quantitatively clustered into distinct drought risk tiers via DBSCAN. Zone-tailored GRU architectures are then trained on a multi-source fusion of hydro-environmental and anthropogenic drivers to forecast monthly SRI and DDV time series in Stage 1, and derive four operational event-level drought metrics—duration, cumulative deficit volume, maximum monthly deficit, and termination rate—in Stage 2. Empirical findings reveal that Stage 1 predictions achieve exceptional accuracy, with coefficient of determination (R 2 ) values exceeding 0.96, Pearson correlation coefficients (PC) above 0.97, and Mean Relative Errors (MRE) reaching as low as 0.039 for deficit volume estimation. Crucially, incorporating prior risk regionalization reduces prediction errors for second-stage event-level metrics by 65% to 82% compared to conventional non-classified GRU models, with R 2 values consistently remaining above 0.97 across all risk categories. Furthermore, the trained deep learning engine achieves a 175 times computational speedup over full SWAT physical simulations, processing 50 years of basin-wide data in just 14.2 s while maintaining high spatial fidelity. By effectively bridging continuous index projections with actionable event-scale recovery metrics, this risk-partitioned framework offers a robust, computationally efficient tool for real-time reservoir dispatch and disaster mitigation.

items.title: Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence for Assessment Support in Higher Education: An Extended UTAUT Approach
items.abstract: AI adoption in higher education assessment has accelerated rapidly worldwide. Despite this widespread uptake, ethical dimensions of AI-assisted assessment remain conceptually underdeveloped, particularly within existing technology-acceptance frameworks that conflate ethical and responsible use. This study aims to examine the factors influencing students' intention and actual behaviour in using AI ethically for assessment support, by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with three ethics-specific constructs: Ethical AI Literacy, Perceived Risk, and Perceived Accountability, alongside the core constructs. The study employed a quantitative cross-sectional design, collecting data from 267 higher education students in London and analysing the data using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4.1. The model explained 64.2% of the variance in Behavioural Intention (R²=0.642) and 47.4% of the variance in Actual Ethical AI Use Behaviour (R²=0.474). Results revealed that Ethical AI Literacy was the strongest predictor of actual behaviour (β=0.410, p<0.001), while Performance Expectancy (β=0.279, p<0.001) and Perceived Risk (β=0.249, p<0.001) shaped intention more strongly than conduct, with Perceived Risk exerting a significant negative effect on actual behaviour (β=-0.257, p<0.001). Behavioural Intention significantly predicted actual behaviour (β=0.235, p=0.002) and significantly mediated the effects of Performance Expectancy, Facilitating Conditions, and Perceived Accountability. These findings suggest that institutions should prioritise ethical AI literacy interventions over compliance-based or risk-focused approaches to meaningfully improve students' ethical AI use in assessment.
